articles.body:
E very time Taylor Swift makes a public appearance, fans pay close attention to her every move , especially the details that may not be obvious at first glance. The singer is known for leaving easter eggs for Swifties to decode , with fans constantly looking for clues about what could be coming next.

However, when Swift was celebrated by the Grammys at an event commemorating her 20 years in the music industry, f ans could not focus entirely on the easter eggs because something shiny appeared to steal the spotlight.

Swift’s rings quickly became the main attraction

The event was a Grammys-organized conversation with Swift about her 20-year career in the music industry, as well as the lyrics and songwriting behind her songs, starting with her country roots. A performance was also expected, and Swift took the stage for a piano-set medley of her songs, including “I Knew It, I Knew You,” “August” and “All Too Well.”

Swift’s rings became the stars of the night because it was the first time fans could see them together in such detail. As she played the piano that accompanied her throughout The Eras Tour, her hands were clearly visible, putting the sparkle of her engagement ring and wedding band on full display.

The close-up gave fans their best look at the rings since her engagement

During the performance, Swift’s wedding ring was seen alongside her old mine cut diamond engagement ring by Kindred Lubeck . The rings took center stage when the camera captured a close-up of her hands, giving fans their closest look at the jewelry since her engagement to Travis Kelce.

Swift’s fans have always enjoyed breaking down the details of her life and career, and her wedding remains one of the biggest moments they continue to follow . With many details from the day still unrevealed, getting a glimpse of the rings offered fans a small hope that they might one day learn more about what happened inside Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes shows his anxiety to return with a telling move on the sideline
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs QB may be ready to get back to work
articles.summary: The Chiefs QB may be ready to get back to work
articles.body:
The NFL season opener is almost here, but the questions surrounding Patrick Mahomes remain unanswered . There is still no set date for his return to the field and no certainty that he will be alongside his teammates when the Chiefs open their 2026 campaign.

Andy Reid has yet to give Mahomes the green light , and there is a clear reason for it. There was no need to take risks with the quarterback during the preseason after a serious injury kept him sidelined for months. The start of the regular season could even come too soon for Mahomes, meaning a Week 1 return is far from guaranteed.

Mahomes’ impatience is becoming harder to miss.

The uncertainty has only made his eagerness to return more noticeable, especially his need to have the football in his hands again. That became clear during a recent moment on the sideline when a football landed near him. Mahomes caught it and immediately started making fakes as if he were back in the middle of the action, offering a glimpse of just how ready he is to return.

Mahomes has been a strong presence during practices, but in Reid’s eyes, it is still too early to start taking risks. Even if Mahomes is anxious to get back, the Chiefs have to keep a clear head and make the decision that is best for the team.

Kansas City still has a major decision to make before Week 1

With the preseason winding down and the Chiefs’ 2026 opener getting closer, Mahomes’ status remains one of the biggest questions surrounding the team.

Kansas City will open its campaign with a Monday Night Football matchup against the defending AFC West champion Denver Broncos on September 14 at Arrowhead Stadium , a game many expect could be the perfect stage for Mahomes to return to the action. However, nothing is guaranteed, even as Reid believes Mahomes could receive the green light for the season and home opener.

articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs received a concerning update during their preparation for the 2026 season . Star running back Kenneth Walker III missed Tuesday’s practice due to a foot injury, just as the team prepares to close out a winless preseason against the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks .

The report was first shared by ESPN’s Nate Taylor , who revealed on X , formerly known as Twitter, that the reigning Super Bowl LX MVP was not expected to take part in the practice session.

“The Chiefs say Kenneth Walker III (foot) is expected to not practice today.”

Walker’s injury is now a situation to monitor closely for Kansas City, with the regular season approaching. The running back joined the Chiefs during the offseason after spending four seasons with Seattle, where he established himself as one of the NFL’s most explosive players at his position.

During the 2025 season , Walker recorded 1,027 rushing yards on 221 carries, averaging 4.6 yards per attempt while scoring five touchdowns. His performance played a key role in Seattle’s historic championship run, which ended with a Super Bowl LX victory and Walker earning Super Bowl MVP honors.

The Chiefs will face Seattle on Friday at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN in their preseason finale. Kansas City enters the matchup after suffering a 16-15 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Saturday.

Once the preseason concludes, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will turn their attention to their regular-season opener against the Denver Broncos , scheduled for Monday, Sept. 14, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Walker’s recovery from the foot injury will be closely monitored as the start of the season draws near.

articles.title: Taylor Swift breaks her silence on her “unmanageable” fame and takes a dig at her critics months after her wedding to Travis Kelce
articles.standfirst: The pop superstar opened up about handling relentless scrutiny while reflecting on why she continues to choose music
articles.summary: The pop superstar opened up about handling relentless scrutiny while reflecting on why she continues to choose music
articles.body:
T aylor Swift has offered a candid look at how she deals with the enormous level of attention surrounding her, admitting that criticism can sometimes become fuel for her creativity.

The 36-year-old singer addressed the pressures that have accompanied her career during an intimate conversation with Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. as part of the Grammy Museum’s The Icon Sessions with Taylor Swift: A 20-Year Retrospective. The discussion, filmed on August 18, gave Swift an opportunity to reflect on the unusual reality of becoming one of the most recognizable people in the world.

Rather than suggesting she has learned to ignore criticism completely, Swift acknowledged that she occasionally enjoys turning the negativity back on those who direct it toward her.

“Sometimes it fuels it. Like sometimes when people are mocking me, it's really fun to mock them back,” the star said.

She followed that up with another pointed observation about the way she chooses to respond.

“Sometimes I like to just use words that they have to look up in order to talk s**t about,” Swift said.

The comments offered a glimpse of the more playful side of Swift's approach to criticism. Over the course of her career, she has faced intense scrutiny over everything from her songwriting and relationships to her public image, while her enormous fanbase has frequently magnified both praise and backlash.

Yet Swift said she has developed a way of reminding herself why she accepted that level of exposure in the first place.

“I go through several processes and coping mechanisms that I've gone through over the years. And one of them is saying, "You chose this. You chose this every day. You could have opted out of this any day before it got unmanageably big."”

“And I decided not to because I love it that much. And that's just where it begins and where it ends. And everything that comes with this ultimately is worth it as long as I get to still make music,” she continued.

Swift makes clear that music remains the priority

Swift's comments suggest that, despite the scale of her fame, the creative process remains the central reason she has continued pursuing a career in music.

She explained that achieving universal approval is not realistic and that her relationship with her audience has become more important than trying to satisfy every critic.

“It's like, anything you say, they're like, "Oh, easy for you to say,"” Swift said, mimicking one of the familiar responses she encounters.

She also explained that her motivation comes from the people who genuinely connect with her work: “I realized that I'm making music because I'm playing for the fans. I'm putting this out for people who care about it and who look to music as a way to cope with their life in the way that I did.”

Swift added: “And I think that if you can actually go through all those checkpoints and realize that putting out music you've made that you love so much is not the path to universal validation... if you're still doing it, then you love it for the right reasons. That's serious.”

The event also marked a significant moment in Swift's personal life. It came only weeks after she married Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce at Madison Square Garden on July 3.

The couple's wedding remained largely private despite an enormous celebrity guest list. Kelce later described the celebration as “the best night of my life” and called it a “crazy night” filled with celebration.

Swift , meanwhile, subtly acknowledged her new status during the Grammy Museum appearance by wearing her wedding band alongside her engagement ring.

Her performance was another highlight of the evening. Sitting at the piano, she delivered a medley featuring “I Knew It, I Knew You,” “August” and “All Too Well.” The performance was particularly notable because it represented her first public performance since the wedding.

The singer also reflected on what songwriting means to her beyond fame and celebrity.

“I never turned to music to forget my human experience,” Swift shared. “I turned to music to remember it. And so in songwriting, I find myself drawn to consequences, stakes, and the passage of time so we can see those decisions through.”

The Grammy Museum appearance therefore became more than another public event for Swift. It offered an unusually personal explanation of how she has managed the weight of extraordinary fame while continuing to create music on her own terms.

Even after reaching a level of celebrity where virtually every decision can become a headline, Swift's message was straightforward: the attention may be overwhelming at times, but as long as she can continue making music she believes in, she considers the trade-off worthwhile.

D olly Parton had a memorable way of responding to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce ’s generosity.

Just hours before the couple’s reported wedding celebration in July, the country music legend recorded a video message thanking them for a $2 million donation to her Imagination Library, before making a joke that immediately captured fans’ attention.

articles.title: No one is safe: A look inside Andy Reid's reasons for reprimanding Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce behind closed doors
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs coach believes even superstars need to be challenged
articles.summary: The Chiefs coach believes even superstars need to be challenged
articles.body:
A ndy Reid has spent years building one of the NFL’s most successful teams around players such as Patrick Mahomes , Travis Kelce and Chris Jones .

Yet the Kansas City Chiefs head coach has made it clear that reputation does not earn anyone a free pass inside the locker room.

Reid recently offered a glimpse into his coaching philosophy during an appearance on Coach2Coach with Jason Garrett , explaining that he is willing to challenge even the biggest names on his roster when he believes they can perform at a higher level.

That includes Mahomes , the three-time Super Bowl-winning quarterback who has become the face of the franchise.

“At times I’m gonna go after (players). I’ll go after Pat Mahomes , the best quarterback in football,” said Reid.

“You have to be able to do this. I know you can. And I’ve seen you do it, and that’s an example to the other guys that, as great as he is, Chris Jones, as great as you are, Travis Kelce, as great as you are, there’s always room to be better. And to be great as a team, we’ve got to be able to do these things. And if you can do them, surely these other guys can that are trying to become as great as you.”

For Reid , the purpose of those conversations is not to embarrass players or undermine their confidence. Instead, he views criticism as another tool for development, particularly when working with players who already operate at an elite level.

Why Reid refuses to treat his stars differently

The distinction Reid makes between criticism and belittling is central to his approach. He wants his players to understand that being established as one of the best at their position does not mean their development has stopped.

“I think it’s important,” said Reid , and then clarified how he approaches players. “But I’m not a belittler. I’m a coach; I’m gonna try to give them things that help them become greater than they are. So it’s not belittling because I think they’re trying to be great. They’re not doing things not to be great, but just a reminder: you’re as great as you are because you did this.”

That philosophy can be particularly valuable in Kansas City, where younger players are constantly watching Mahomes and Kelce . If Reid can demand more from established stars, he can establish a standard that applies throughout the roster.

Mahomes ’ current situation also demonstrates why Reid’s judgment extends beyond simply demanding maximum effort. The quarterback is working his way back from significant knee injuries involving his ACL and LCL, making his eventual return a carefully managed decision.

Mahomes has previously expressed his desire to return to action as soon as possible, including after Kansas City’s 16-15 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Ultimately, however, Reid has emphasized that the final decision on when his quarterback returns belongs to the coaching staff.

That balance between demanding more and knowing when to protect a player is an important part of Reid’s relationship with Mahomes .

The same principle applies to Kelce and the rest of Kansas City’s veterans. No matter how accomplished a player becomes, Reid believes there is always another detail to sharpen, another assignment to execute better and another opportunity to raise the team's overall standard.

For the Chiefs , that mentality could prove crucial as they attempt to regain their position atop the AFC West.

Reid is not simply relying on the talent of his stars. He is challenging them to set the example, while making sure that even the most decorated players understand they remain accountable.

In Reid’s locker room, apparently, nobody is too important to receive a little coaching.

articles.title: Chiefs Official: Patrick Mahomes ruled out for Friday's game against Seattle; rookie Garrett Nussmeier will start
articles.standfirst: Kansas City is keeping its franchise quarterback on the sideline as his recovery from major knee surgery continues
articles.summary: Kansas City is keeping its franchise quarterback on the sideline as his recovery from major knee surgery continues
articles.body:
P atrick Mahomes will not take the field when the Kansas City Chiefs close out their preseason against the Seattle Seahawks on Friday, with head coach Andy Reid confirming that rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier will get the start instead.

The decision provides another indication that Kansas City remains unwilling to take unnecessary chances with Mahomes as he works his way back from the serious knee injuries he suffered last season.

Mahomes underwent surgery to repair torn ACL and LCL ligaments in December, beginning a lengthy rehabilitation process that has continued throughout the offseason.

Despite the extended recovery, Mahomes has made encouraging progress during training camp. He has participated consistently since being cleared to practice and has not needed to miss a session because of the knee.

The Chiefs have also been able to watch him work through increasingly demanding practice situations, giving the coaching staff a clearer picture of his readiness for the regular season.

Mahomes himself said earlier this week that his recovery was continuing in the right direction. The three-time Super Bowl MVP had previously made it clear that he would like to see some preseason action if Reid believed the timing was appropriate. That opportunity will not come against Seattle.

The Chiefs ' approach is consistent with the bigger picture. Kansas City has been treating the preseason as part of Mahomes ' rehabilitation rather than a deadline for him to prove he can play.

With the regular-season opener against the Denver Broncos scheduled for Sept. 14, there is still time for the quarterback to complete the final stages of his comeback.

Garrett Nussmeier gets another opportunity to impress

Instead of Mahomes , the spotlight will shift to Nussmeier , the seventh-round selection Kansas City made with the 249th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

The former LSU quarterback has already received meaningful preseason snaps and will now have another chance to strengthen his position before the Chiefs finalize their roster.

Nussmeier has completed 22 of 36 passes for 172 yards across Kansas City's first two preseason games.

He has shown enough for the Chiefs to give him another extended opportunity, particularly with Chris Oladokun unavailable for the finale.

His first two appearances have included 13 completions on 19 attempts for 98 yards against the Los Angeles Rams , followed by nine completions on 17 attempts for 74 yards against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

The rookie has also been getting valuable work in practice alongside Mahomes and the rest of Kansas City's quarterback room.

The Chiefs ' official practice reports have highlighted Nussmeier's arm talent, including a touchdown connection with wide receiver Jacob DeJesus during an 11-on-11 period.

That experience could become particularly important if Nussmeier earns a roster spot as the season approaches.

Friday's game will give him another opportunity to demonstrate that he can operate the offense efficiently while playing against an opponent that is also preparing for the regular season.

Mahomes ' absence, meanwhile, means the two-time MVP will complete the preseason without appearing in a game.

That is unusual for a quarterback of his stature, but the circumstances make the decision understandable given the severity of his previous injuries. The Chiefs have already seen enough from him in practice to remain confident in his progression.

Kansas City is scheduled to host Seattle at Arrowhead Stadium on Friday night, with kickoff set for 7 p.m. CT.

For the Chiefs , the result of the preseason finale will matter far less than having Mahomes ready when the games begin to count.

The organization is clearly prioritizing his long-term health, while Nussmeier now has one more opportunity to make his case before Kansas City turns its full attention toward the Sept. 14 opener.

At this stage, Mahomes does not need a preseason game to prove what he can do. The Chiefs' priority is making sure the quarterback is physically prepared for the demands of another NFL season, and Reid's latest decision suggests the team believes patience remains the best way to get there.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' text messages to Brittany give the Chiefs hope ahead of Week 1
articles.standfirst: Poor cell service has made the QB hard to reach, but Brittany still hears from him
articles.summary: Poor cell service has made the QB hard to reach, but Brittany still hears from him
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes has spent this summer buried in one of the most demanding stretches of his NFL career, balancing training camp with a relentless rehabilitation schedule as he works his way back from an ACL injury. That routine hasn't left much room for casual phone time.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback joked Tuesday that cell service inside the team’s dorms at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph is unreliable enough that he has barely been texting anyone during camp. There is one person he makes sure to reach.

“St. Joe’s dorm rooms, man, you don’t get a lot of text messages,” Mahomes told reporters. “I just try to make sure I text Brittany. If I text Brittany, I’m usually in a good spot.”

The comment came when Mahomes was asked whether he had been messaging Zach Ertz , who also suffered an ACL injury shortly before him.

“I haven’t been texting him during camp. I’ve been locked in throughout camp, but I know he’s still working,” Mahomes said. “I saw him throwing... I know he’s working too.”

Mahomes’ rehab becomes full-time job

The light moment with reporters came against the backdrop of an unusually intense offseason.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid said earlier this month that Mahomes has been spending “seven hours a day” working on his recovery.

“He just goes,” Reid told CBS Sports. “He kept playing, he gets his rehab taken care of before and after practice, you know how he is, he’s all in.”

Reid also made clear that Kansas City has been careful not to let its quarterback push too far.

“He’s a great example to all the other guys around him that, ‘I’m gonna do whatever I have to do to get myself on the field,’” Reid said.

That urgency comes after a difficult year in Kansas City, with the Chiefs finishing 6-11 and missing the playoffs for the first time in a decade.

Brittany and family remain part of Mahomes’ perspective

Even as football has consumed much of his daily schedule, Mahomes has repeatedly said his family helps keep the sport in perspective.

“Football is a huge part of my life, but I’ve always tried to keep perspective,” Mahomes told PEOPLE. “Family, friends, my teammates, my foundation work, those things have always been important to me.”

He added: “During the season you’re so locked in, so having that time to slow down, be present with the kids, and just enjoy the people around you makes it special.”

Mahomes and Brittany have three children, and the quarterback said that responsibility remains closely tied to the way he approaches his career.

“I want to be the best for my family, my teammates, the kids who look up to this game,” Mahomes said.

Camp may have him spending hours on rehab, meetings and practice, with barely enough cell service to maintain a normal conversation. But one message, apparently, remains non-negotiable.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes' toned physique has Kelly Stafford obsessed
articles.standfirst: Stafford’s latest Instagram reaction has taken the joke to another level.
articles.summary: Stafford’s latest Instagram reaction has taken the joke to another level.
articles.body:
Kelly Stafford has found a new recurring theme on Instagram, and Brittany Mahomes is at the center of it.

Within days, Stafford twice reposted workout content from Mahomes and added captions that went well beyond a routine compliment. The first was brief - “Kinda chic to build muscle.” The second was even more direct.

“Sooo does the body come with the set @brittanylynne.. asking for a friend,” Stafford wrote alongside another Adidas gym post from Mahomes .

Taken together, the comments have started to look less like isolated reactions and more like a running joke between two women who are already close.

Stafford has backed Mahomes before

The dynamic makes more sense with some context.

Stafford , the wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford , has previously spoken highly of Mahomes and defended her publicly when criticism followed her Sports Illustrated Swimsuit appearance.

She has described Mahomes as one of the women she looks up to, alongside Kristin Juszczyk , and has argued that having a large platform is not something women should feel embarrassed about.

That history matters because the latest posts do not read as random commentary from the sidelines. They fit a relationship in which Stafford has repeatedly shown support for Mahomes , just this time with considerably more humor.

It also fits Stafford’s broader online personality. She has built a reputation for being candid, self-aware and willing to say the thing most people would leave in a private chat.

Mahomes’ profile goes far beyond Patrick Mahomes

Brittany Mahomes has become one of the most recognizable figures around the NFL, but her public profile is not simply tied to husband Patrick Mahomes .

She is a co-owner of the Kansas City Current and has played a visible role in the club’s growth, including the development of a stadium built specifically for a women’s professional sports team.

That mix of fitness, business and football-adjacent celebrity has also made Mahomes a major figure in the growing social-media ecosystem around NFL wives and partners.

Women connected to players increasingly promote each other’s brands, model clothing lines and turn Instagram comments into their own form of public conversation. Stafford’s two posts fit neatly into that world.

articles.standfirst: Ava Hunt is back at SMU and celebrating her return to the cheerleading squad.
articles.summary: Ava Hunt is back at SMU and celebrating her return to the cheerleading squad.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs heiress Ava Hunt is back in uniform after returning to Southern Methodist University and rejoining the school's cheerleading squad for the 2026 season.

Hunt , the youngest daughter of Chiefs owner Clark Hunt , appeared alongside her SMU teammates in a series of new photos as preparations continued for the upcoming college football campaign.

The pictures were shared by her friend and fellow cheerleader Cheyanna Frazier , showing Hunt smiling alongside other members of the Mustangs squad during media day.

“We are SO back,” Frazier wrote alongside the post.

Ava Hunt returns to SMU cheerleading

Hunt originally joined the SMU cheerleading team during her freshman year in 2024, but later stepped away from college for a year.

Instead of immediately continuing her studies and cheerleading commitments, she devoted time to faith-based humanitarian work through the Discipleship Training School in Kona, Hawaii.

Her return means Hunt will once again balance college life with her position on the SMU squad, putting her back on the sidelines as the new season begins.

The latest photos showed Hunt wearing her SMU cheerleading uniform alongside Frazier and several teammates at University Park, Texas.

Her return also comes after a busy summer away from campus. Hunt was spotted with her older sister Gracie at the 2026 World Cup last month before heading back to college.

Chiefs heiress remains closely connected to NFL

Although Hunt is building her own profile through college and cheerleading, her family remains one of the most recognizable in the NFL.

articles.standfirst: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are learning how to balance married life with two demanding careers.
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are learning how to balance married life with two demanding careers.
articles.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are reportedly settling into a new rhythm after getting married, with both adapting to the realities of balancing their relationship with demanding careers.

The couple, who tied the knot earlier this year, are said to be working out what their day-to-day life looks like now that the excitement of the wedding has passed.

Their schedules remain one of the biggest challenges. Swift continues to manage a packed professional calendar, while Kelce is preparing for another NFL season with the Kansas City Chiefs .

That means married life hasn't necessarily brought a slower pace, with the pair instead learning how to fit their personal time around work commitments.

Swift and Kelce adjust to a new routine

According to Page Six, the couple are "figuring out their new normal" as newlyweds.

Their relationship has always required careful planning because of the demands placed on both of them, but marriage has introduced a different kind of routine.

Swift has spent years moving between recording, touring and other projects, while Kelce's football schedule involves training, travel and weekly games during the season.

The pair have nevertheless made a point of supporting each other's careers throughout their relationship.

Swift became a regular presence at Chiefs games, while Kelce attended several Eras Tour shows before their wedding.

Married life still shaped by busy careers

The couple's ability to spend extended stretches together could become more difficult once the NFL season begins.

Kelce's commitments with Kansas City will increase significantly, while Swift is expected to continue working on music and other projects of her own.

Despite that, their relationship has already been built around long periods apart and carefully planned reunions.

That experience may help them as they adjust to married life without expecting either person to step away from their career.

For Swift and Kelce , the challenge now appears to be less about changing their lives completely and more about finding ways to make two unusually demanding schedules work together.

Their marriage may have marked a major personal milestone, but professionally, very little has slowed down.

For now, the newlyweds are reportedly focused on finding a routine that allows them to protect their relationship while continuing to pursue the careers that made them two of the most recognizable figures in entertainment and sport.

articles.title: How Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes plan to turn play action into a powerful weapon
articles.standfirst: Kansas City believes a more convincing play action game can help revive its offense in 2026.
articles.summary: Kansas City believes a more convincing play action game can help revive its offense in 2026.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid are looking to make deception a much bigger part of the Kansas City Chiefs offense after a disappointing 2025 season exposed weaknesses in their running game.

Kansas City finished 6-11 and missed the playoffs for the first time in Mahomes ’ career, with the quarterback’s season also ending early because of ACL and LCL injuries.

One of the areas Reid and Mahomes have focused on during training camp is making play action more effective by giving defenses a genuine reason to respect the run.

Mahomes changes how he sells the fake

Mahomes operated from shotgun on 80.6 percent of Kansas City’s non-kneel-down snaps last season, the third-highest rate in the NFL.

That could now change following the arrival of Kenneth Walker III , whose running style gives the Chiefs more reason to work from under center.

“No. 9. That’s all I can say,” Mahomes said when asked what excited him most about the offense. “That change and the ability to catch, run, pass protect, do everything. [He can] make a play out of nothing into a 20-yard gain. That’s going to be the biggest impact, I think, we’ll have — just finding the ways to get him the ball.”

Mahomes has also been working on keeping the ball visible for longer during play fakes and bringing it closer to the running back.

Last season, he sometimes pulled the ball back too quickly, allowing linebackers to recognize that a pass was coming.

Reid wants play action to actually fool defenses

Reid has made clear that simply calling more play action isn’t enough.

“Well, play-action has always been a big part of this offense,” Reid said. “We look at the production of it. What are you getting out of it [on film]? You might as well just dropback and forget about the play-action.”

Kansas City has experimented with several variations during camp, including deeper drops, rollouts and less conventional fakes involving receivers in motion.

The idea is to make every fake look more like a genuine handoff, forcing linebackers and safeties to hesitate before reacting.

Travis Kelce has also praised Mahomes ’ approach ahead of the new season.

“Pat has done an unbelievable job of not only getting himself ready, but working with these receivers and making sure that everybody’s living up to that standard of how we’re going to play this year,” Kelce said.

If Kansas City can make defenses believe the run is coming, Reid and Mahomes could regain some of the space their passing attack lost last season.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs break new ground with an unprecedented move before the season
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs will kick off the season at home against the Broncos in the first Monday Night game of the season
articles.summary: The Chiefs will kick off the season at home against the Broncos in the first Monday Night game of the season
articles.body:
The NFL preseason reaches its finish line this weekend, meaning that the real action is under two weeks away, beginning with the opening game of the regular season, a Super Bowl rematch between the defending champion Seattle Seahawks and the New England Patriots at the champions' home venue, Lumen Field .

Notably, the Seahawks enter a brand-new era under new owners in the Khosla family , who purchased the franchise for an NFL-record $9.612 billion .

As the campaign draws closer, one of the most compelling storylines is how the Kansas City Chiefs plan to bounce back after experiencing their worst campaign since 2012 , which marked the first time in Patrick Mahomes ' career that he missed the playoffs following eight consecutive seasons as an opening-day starter, a stellar run featuring three Super Bowl rings .

Patrick Mahomes Sidelined for Entire Preseason

Throughout the first two games of the preseason, Mahomes has seen zero game action while continuing his structured recovery from a severe ACL and LCL tear suffered last December.

For the final exhibition matchup at Arrowhead Stadium against the Seahawks, head coach Andy Reid confirmed that rookie signal-caller Garrett Nussmeier would get the start and potentially play the entire contest after Chris Oladokun , who was initially expected to share reps, entered the concussion protocol.

This milestone marks the first time in Mahomes' professional life that he will not play a single snap during the preseason , a possibility Reid hinted at weeks ago by noting, "I mean, there's a pretty good chance where I don't play him."

While the superstar quarterback undoubtedly wanted to test his knee at full speed against live opposition before the high-stakes Monday Night Football opener against the Denver Broncos , their fiercest division rival following a shift that ended Kansas City's streak of nine consecutive division titles, ultimate caution prevailed within the coaching staff.

Rebuilding the Offensive Engine With Familiar Faces and Fresh Firepower

With zero preseason reps under his belt, all eyes will be glued to how Mahomes performs upon returning from his December 2025 injury setback. Statistically, his production dipped over the final three seasons prior to his absence, with none surpassing 27 touchdown passes or 4,200 passing yards , modest figures compared to the historic, record-shattering heights of his early years.

A major reason for optimism, alongside a boosted ground attack featuring Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III , is the triumphant return of former offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy to Kansas City.

Bieniemy was right by Mahomes' side during his first five seasons as a starter, a golden era where the quarterback played the best football of his life, hoisting two Lombardi Trophies, claiming a pair of MVP awards , and averaging nearly 5,000 passing yards alongside 38 touchdowns per season.

articles.title: Crucial Chiefs player has become a serious doubt with season nearing, making Patrick Mahomes sweat bullets
articles.standfirst: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid doesn't like what's going on at the moment.
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid doesn't like what's going on at the moment.
articles.body:
In order for the Kansas City Chiefs to truly bounce back in 2026, just about everything has to go right. Patrick Mahomes and Rashee Rice have to be fully healthy, Travis Kelce has to turn back the clock, the team's defensive additions need to gel together.

Despite the Chiefs having plenty of question marks around the roster, head coach Andy Reid could at least hang his hat on the offensive line being one of the better units in the NFL. The interior of the o-line is stacked with talent, as are the tackle positions. But talent isn't enough sometimes.

The Chiefs are finding that out the hard way with left tackle Josh Simmons . The team's first round pick last year had a rollercoaster rookie season, which included speeding back from knee surgery to start in Week 1, taking a break from the team mid-season due to a family situation, and overall not performing overly well when on the field .

Chiefs fans growing worried about Josh Simmons' situation with the Chiefs

But given Simmons' immense talent, he's fully expected to hold down the left tackle spot this season and for years to come. The only way that can happen is if he's on the field . Right now, that isn't the case, as Simmons has been sidelined by a back injury . While reports from local beat writers suggest the Chiefs aren't concerned with Simmons' injury, it sounds like they might be concerned with how he's handling it .

According to Chase Snyder , Simmons is the one who chose to undergo further testing . While the Chiefs believe it's minor, Simmons is being cautious and taking all measures to make sure he's completely fine . Some fans noted Reid seemed a little perturbed when asked about Simmons' injury in a recent press conference.

While this is being made into a bigger deal due to Simmons' prolonged absence last season, which was considered " mysterious " at the time, the player is likely fine and should play sooner than later.

Regardless, it's not ideal for the team's young left tackle to be out of practice . He needs reps to improve and develop, especially in a season where Mahomes needs more protection than usual.

articles.title: Is Travis Kelce already more focused on business than the NFL? Inside his $90 million empire before a possible Chiefs farewell
articles.standfirst: A growing business portfolio is already giving Travis Kelce plenty of options beyond football.
articles.summary: A growing business portfolio is already giving Travis Kelce plenty of options beyond football.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce may still be preparing for another season with the Kansas City Chiefs , but the tight end has already built a business empire that could make retirement from the NFL considerably easier.

With speculation continuing that the 2026 campaign could be Kelce's final season , his interests outside football are receiving increasing attention.

His growing portfolio reportedly includes media projects, investments, endorsements and the hugely successful New Heights podcast he hosts with brother Jason Kelce .

Travis Kelce builds life beyond the Chiefs

The brothers struck a major deal with Amazon's Wondery in 2024 for New Heights, with the agreement reportedly worth more than $100 million over three years.

Kelce has also expanded his presence in entertainment.

His acting credits include appearances in Grotesquerie and Happy Gilmore 2, while he also hosted the game show Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity?

Those opportunities have allowed Kelce to build a public profile extending far beyond his success with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs .

His business interests reportedly contribute to an estimated net worth of around $90 million, giving him substantial financial security whenever his football career ends.

Could 2026 be Kelce's final NFL season?

Kelce has yet to officially announce plans to retire after the season, but questions about his future have followed him as he enters another year in Kansas City.

The veteran has already acknowledged that he thinks about how long he can continue playing at the required level.

“I think about it every single day,” Kelce previously said when discussing retirement. “It’s a decision that I’m going to have to make at some point.”

For now, however, his focus remains on helping Kansas City compete.

“I love football,” Kelce has said. “I love coming into work every single day.”

That commitment hasn't prevented him from preparing for what comes next.

Kelce has invested in several businesses and brands while establishing himself as one of the NFL's most recognizable personalities away from the field.

Whether he decides to leave the Chiefs after 2026 remains uncertain, but financially and professionally, his post-NFL career appears to be taking shape long before he plays his final snap.

articles.title: Emotional Travis Kelce soaks in the moment before Chiefs’ preseason finale as questions about his future linger
articles.standfirst: One of the greatest tight ends of all time knows that his career could be over soon
articles.summary: One of the greatest tight ends of all time knows that his career could be over soon
articles.body:
Travis Kelce has been one of the defining figures of the Kansas City Chiefs dynasty . He has caught touchdown passes in Super Bowls, shattered records at the tight end position, and helped transform Kansas City into the NFL's gold standard.

On Friday night, however, one of the most memorable moments involving the future Hall of Famer came before the opening kickoff. As the national anthem played ahead of the Chiefs' final preseason game against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, Kelce appeared visibly emotional while taking in the atmosphere.

For a player entering what could potentially be the final season of his remarkable NFL career, it was a moment that seemed to carry extra significance. The veteran tight end stood on the sideline soaking in the scene as Arrowhead Stadium prepared for one last tune-up before the regular season begins. Whether or not this ultimately proves to be Kelce's final campaign , the emotions were understandable.

Appreciating every moment

At 36 years old, Kelce has little left to prove. His résumé already includes multiple Super Bowl championships, countless postseason records, and a place among the greatest tight ends in NFL history. Year after year, he has remained one of Patrick Mahomes' most trusted targets and one of the most recognizable faces in the sport.

Yet even the greatest careers eventually come to an end. That reality has fueled speculation throughout the offseason about how much longer Kelce intends to play. While he has not announced any retirement plans, every game now carries an added layer of significance for fans who understand that opportunities to watch him in a Chiefs uniform may be limited.

While the pregame moment reflected the seriousness of the occasion, Kelce's competitive spirit and enthusiasm quickly returned once the game began. One of the night's most entertaining plays came when fellow tight end Tre Watson hauled in a pass and hurdled a Seattle defender in spectacular fashion.

Cameras caught Kelce reacting instantly, popping up with a small celebratory jump as he watched his teammate make the highlight-reel play. It was a classic Kelce reaction. Throughout his career, teammates have praised his energy and passion for the game.

Whether he is making a clutch catch himself or celebrating someone else's success, Kelce has long been one of the emotional leaders inside Kansas City's locker room. That excitement remained evident against Seattle.

articles.title: Taylor Swift sends $50,000 and a heartfelt message to a mother who nearly died saving some teenagers
articles.standfirst: Swift donates $50,000 after mother suffers life-threatening injuries protecting teens
articles.summary: Swift donates $50,000 after mother suffers life-threatening injuries protecting teens
articles.body:
Taylor Swift has donated $50,000 to support Ashley Taunton , a Connecticut mother of three who suffered devastating injuries after risking her own life to protect teenagers involved in a highway crash.

The 42-year-old was driving south on Interstate 95 in Rhode Island with her youngest daughter on July 18 when she spotted three teenagers whose vehicle had hydroplaned during a powerful rainstorm. Instead of passing the scene, the certified nursing assistant pulled over to see if she could help.

“When I see there’s somebody in trouble, I tend to want to go help,” Taunton told People.

She parked roughly 30 yards from the crash and instructed her daughter to remain safely inside their vehicle. Taunton then approached the teenagers, who appeared shaken and had sustained some injuries but initially seemed to be relatively okay.

The situation quickly became far more dangerous. Another vehicle traveling along the rain-soaked highway lost control and began heading toward Taunton and the teenagers. Realizing one of the young people was directly in the vehicle’s path, Taunton reacted immediately.

She pushed the teenager out of harm’s way, but she couldn't escape the approaching vehicle herself.

The collision left Taunton with severe, potentially fatal injuries. She suffered multiple broken ribs, internal bleeding, injuries to her liver and spleen, and a ruptured diaphragm.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes surprises fans with an unexpected twist in her game-day style
articles.standfirst: A double-denim look and matching sneakers give Brittany Mahomes’ game-day style a fresh twist
articles.summary: A double-denim look and matching sneakers give Brittany Mahomes’ game-day style a fresh twist
articles.body:
Brittany Mahomes brought a surprisingly stylish twist to her latest Kansas City Chiefs game-day appearance, stepping away from the team’s familiar red-and-gold color palette for an all-blue look.

The 30-year-old attended Friday’s preseason matchup between the Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium with members of her family.

Although her husband, Patrick Mahomes, didn’t take the field, Brittany still made an impression with a relaxed yet carefully coordinated outfit.

She shared footage from the family’s game-day outing on Instagram, captioning the post, “Straight chaos 😎❤️.” While the evening might have been busy with the family, her outfit looked anything but chaotic.

Brittany opted for a double-denim combination that immediately stood out. She wore a cropped blue denim jacket with matching micro shorts, creating a coordinated look that felt casual while still being fashion-forward.

Underneath the jacket, she added a simple white T-shirt, giving the outfit a clean contrast.

The biggest surprise came with her choice of footwear.

Rather than completing the denim look with neutral or white sneakers, Brittany continued the blue theme with a pair of blue Adidas sneakers. The matching shoes made the color coordination especially noticeable.

She accessorized with rose-colored sunglasses and wore her blonde hair down, straight and parted to the side. Her polished makeup added another touch of glamour without taking away from the laid-back nature of the outfit.

Brittany Mahomes puts a fresh spin on Chiefs game-day fashion

While Brittany opted for a less traditional color scheme, her children embraced the Chiefs’ signature style.

Her daughter Sterling , 5, wore a gray “Chiefs Kingdom” dress, pairing it with a red bow in her hair. Her son Bronze , 3, also represented the team in a red Chiefs-branded polo. Their younger sibling, Golden , 19 months, didn’t appear to attend the game.

The family’s appearance continued Brittany’s long-running tradition of supporting Patrick from the sidelines. Since their relationship began when they were teenagers, she’s remained a visible presence throughout his football career and regularly shares moments from Chiefs game days.

Patrick , meanwhile, watched from the sideline as Kansas City and Seattle played to a 9-9 draw. Neither team managed to create much separation, and the game ultimately came down to a late opportunity for the Seahawks.

Seattle kicker Jason Myers had a chance to win it with a 52-yard field goal as time expired, but his attempt missed.

Although the preseason contest lacked a decisive finish, Brittany’s outfit gave fans something else to talk about. Her choice to trade the Chiefs’ usual red for shades of blue showed that game-day fashion doesn’t always have to follow traditional team colors.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes is over his knee injury but another pain could reshape his Super Bowl story
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs quarterback says the emotional scars of losing the Super Bowl still haven’t faded.
articles.summary: The Chiefs quarterback says the emotional scars of losing the Super Bowl still haven’t faded.
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes may have recovered physically from the knee issue that disrupted part of his season, but the Kansas City Chiefs star admits another kind of pain is still driving him.

The three-time Super Bowl champion has spoken openly about how deeply championship defeats stay with him, describing those losses as defining moments rather than something he can simply move past.

“Anytime you lose a Super Bowl, it’s the worst thing in the world,” Mahomes said. “It will stick with you the rest of your career.”

That frustration now appears to be fueling his approach as Kansas City prepares for another run at the Lombardi Trophy.

Mahomes says Super Bowl losses never disappear

Mahomes has already built one of the most successful resumes of any quarterback of his generation, but his defeats on football’s biggest stage continue to shape how he views his career.

He made clear that the pain of losing doesn’t diminish just because he has also experienced championship success.

“You remember the wins, but the losses, those are the ones that stick with you,” Mahomes said.

That mentality could become particularly important for a Chiefs team attempting to respond after falling short of another title.

Mahomes has repeatedly spoken about using disappointment as motivation, and his latest comments suggest the scars of previous Super Bowl defeats remain very much part of that process.

Chiefs quarterback looks for another title run

Physically, Mahomes has moved beyond concerns surrounding his knee and is once again focused on leading Kansas City through another season.

Mentally, however, the losses continue to provide an edge.

“Every year is a new challenge,” Mahomes said. “You have to find a way to get better and come back stronger.”

That mindset has helped define a career already filled with postseason success, but Mahomes is clearly far from satisfied.

The quarterback knows each failed championship opportunity becomes part of his legacy just as much as the victories.

For Kansas City, that could make his lingering frustration particularly dangerous for the rest of the NFL.

Mahomes no longer has to worry about the knee that once limited him, but the emotional pain of losing a Super Bowl is something he says will never completely disappear.

And if that memory pushes him toward another championship, it could end up changing the story of his career once again.

articles.title: Jason Kelce’s criticism of Travis Kelce’s Chiefs teammate could cool their relationship
articles.standfirst: A blunt assessment of Chiefs star Trey Smith's technique.
articles.summary: A blunt assessment of Chiefs star Trey Smith's technique.
articles.body:
Jason Kelce has publicly picked apart a costly mistake from Kansas City Chiefs guard Trey Smith , despite previously being one of the offensive lineman's biggest admirers.

The former Philadelphia Eagles center reacted after Seattle Seahawks linebacker Jared Ivey got the better of Smith during Kansas City's preseason finale, with Kelce arguing that the problem wasn't strength or talent but technique.

“Trey Smith is a bad man, but it don’t matter how much of a beast you are if you go in with bad technique,” Kelce wrote on X.

“Trey should be striking this kickout block with his left shoulder, and left foot forward. Same foot same shoulder is how power is generated.”

Jason Kelce explains where Trey Smith went wrong

The play came as rookie quarterback Garrett Nussmeier handed the ball to running back Emmett Johnson. Travis Kelce and Smith moved across the formation to execute kickout blocks, but Ivey managed to stop Smith and disrupt the run.

Jason Kelce was just as enthusiastic about Ivey's execution as he was critical of Smith's .

“Conversely we see Jared Ivey striking Trey with perfect technique, right foot forward right shoulder. Ivey is also way lower and does a great job squeezing down the line and catching Trey before he is ready for contact.”

Kelce then made clear that one bad rep hadn't changed his wider opinion of Smith .

“Trey is still a badass, but what F***ing Outstanding rep from Ivey.”

Chiefs counting on Smith after huge contract

The criticism carries extra weight because Smith is one of Kansas City's most important offensive linemen.

The Chiefs handed him a four-year, $94 million extension with $70 million guaranteed, making him the NFL's highest-paid interior lineman at the time of the agreement.

Smith also entered the preseason after missing much of padded training camp work because of a hip injury.

“Trey (Smith) loves to play, but it was important that he let that thing heal up like he did,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after Smith visited a specialist. “And I think it’ll pay off for him down the road.”

Kelce's criticism therefore wasn't a dismissal of Smith's ability. It was a detailed warning from one of the NFL's most accomplished former offensive linemen that even an elite player can lose a rep when his fundamentals aren't right.

articles.title: Taylor Swift is still on the minds of her exes making a surprise appearance in Harry Styles’ thoughts
articles.standfirst: Harry Styles had fans losing it after making a cheeky reference
articles.summary: Harry Styles had fans losing it after making a cheeky reference
articles.body:
A lthough Harry Styles and Taylor Swift dated more than a decade ago, their relationship is now known to be cordial. The two have been seen talking at events and being friendly with each other. Still, every once in a while, Swift finds her way into the minds of her exes, and Harry Styles just said it out loud.

Harry is currently on tour with Together, Together , with one of his longest stops taking place at Madison Square Garden. The iconic venue is not only important to Styles, but also to countless artists who have had the chance to perform there, making Harry well aware of the magnitude of the place and what it means to have a residency there.

Madison Square Garden has seen it all

MSG has been the stage for some of the biggest moments in entertainment history , and Styles knows the privilege of performing in a venue that has welcomed some of the biggest names. During his show, he gave the arena a special mention, recognizing it as the home of the NBA champion New York Knicks before also making a playful reference to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding.

While wrapping up his show as part of his residency at the iconic arena, Styles pointed out that Madison Square Garden is the home of the New York Knicks. He then added with a cheeky grin that the venue also hosts weddings, according to fan-captured footage from the concert.

The arena does a little bit of everything, and Harry acknowledged that in a joking tone. Fans in attendance immediately reacted after Styles referenced one of his exes and recognized that they were standing in the same place connected to one of the most talked-about moments in contemporary pop culture , one that not only brought New York to a standstill but remains one of the biggest mysteries in the entertainment industry.

Harry’s joke hits differently after the wedding invite reports

Styles’ joke is even more interesting considering reports that he was actually invited to Swift and Kelce’s July 3 wedding . The connection goes beyond Harry’s relationship with Zoë Kravitz, who has been friends with Swift for years, as Styles and Swift have also maintained a respectful relationship.

The coincidence is that the singer reportedly could not attend because he was scheduled to perform in London that same night as part of his tour. Now, Styles is performing at the very venue that became the center of attention after the wedding, turning his Madison Square Garden residency into another unexpected connection to one of his most famous exes.

articles.title: From the frenzy in the VIP box to the list of layoffs: The player who drove Taylor Swift wild is officially out of a job
articles.standfirst: The player at the center of one of Taylor Swift’s most memorable Super Bowl celebrations has been cut
articles.summary: The player at the center of one of Taylor Swift’s most memorable Super Bowl celebrations has been cut
articles.body:
Mecole Hardman Jr. has gone from Super Bowl hero to an NFL free agent, with the former Kansas City Chiefs star now facing an uncertain future just days before the 2026 season begins.

The Buffalo Bills released Hardman on Saturday as they continued trimming their roster ahead of the NFL's 53-man deadline. The move brings an abrupt end to his brief spell in Buffalo and leaves the 28-year-old searching for another opportunity.

Hardman's career reached one of its biggest highs in February 2024, when he caught Patrick Mahomes' overtime touchdown pass against the San Francisco 49ers to seal Super Bowl LVIII for Kansas City.

The dramatic score earned Hardman his third Super Bowl championship and produced an unforgettable celebration.

Taylor Swift, watching from the stands as Travis Kelce's partner, made her way onto the field and embraced Hardman after the victory, telling him she was happy for the team.

The connection between Hardman and Swift wasn't limited to that extraordinary night. Hardman previously recalled meeting the pop superstar and performing card tricks for her.

Swift's reaction was reportedly that his magic was “crazy,” a story that became one of the more unusual anecdotes surrounding the Chiefs' famous inner circle.

Hardman's fiancée, Chariah Gordon, also became friendly with Swift during their time around the Chiefs. Gordon has spoken warmly about Swift and described her as kind, fun and genuine.

The two were regularly seen together during Kansas City's championship run, giving Hardman another unexpected link to one of the world's biggest entertainers.

Hardman's NFL future now hangs in the balance

While Hardman's profile grew off the field, his playing career has taken a difficult turn since that Super Bowl triumph.

He returned to Kansas City on a one-year contract after his championship-winning performance but suffered a season-ending knee injury later in 2024. He then moved to the Green Bay Packers in 2025, although he couldn't secure a place on their active roster.

Buffalo offered him another chance. Hardman joined the Bills' practice squad in November 2025 and was later elevated to the active roster. He subsequently returned on a reserve/futures contract in January 2026, hoping his experience as a receiver and return specialist would help him win a roster spot.

He showed some promise during this year's preseason, catching four passes for 20 yards and a touchdown over three games. He also handled return duties, recording three kickoff returns for 80 yards and four punt returns for 50 yards.

That production ultimately wasn't enough. Ray Davis emerged as a preferred option in the return game, while Buffalo faced difficult decisions as it reduced its roster.

Hardman is now available to sign with another team, giving him one more chance to extend a career that once included a Super Bowl-winning play and a memorable celebration with Swift .

articles.title: NFL cuts: Three receivers from the Chiefs’ last Super Bowl winning team were let go
articles.standfirst: It’s a reminder of how ruthless the league can be, even for good players
articles.summary: It’s a reminder of how ruthless the league can be, even for good players
articles.body:
T he NFL loves to celebrate champions. Every February, confetti falls, players lift the Lombardi Trophy, and legacies are cemented. Fans remember the game-winning touchdowns, the clutch catches, and the players who helped deliver a title.

What often gets forgotten is how quickly the league moves on. This weekend provided a stark reminder of that reality when three of the top four wide receivers from the Kansas City Chiefs’ most recent Super Bowl-winning team all found themselves looking for work.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling was released by the Dallas Cowboys, Justin Watson was cut by the Houston Texans, and Mecole Hardman was let go by the Buffalo Bills as teams trimmed their rosters ahead of the regular season. Just a few years ago, all three were important contributors on a championship roster. Today, all three are free agents. That is the NFL.

From champions to roster casualties

The Chiefs' receiving corps was never viewed as the most talented group in football, but it was good enough to help Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid capture a Super Bowl. Valdes-Scantling delivered some of the biggest catches of Kansas City's postseason run. Watson carved out a role as a reliable depth receiver and special teams contributor. Hardman authored one of the most memorable moments in franchise history when he caught the game-winning touchdown in overtime of Super Bowl LVIII.

Those plays are forever, but roster spots are not. Valdes-Scantling entered training camp with Dallas hoping to carve out a role in a crowded receiver room, but ultimately did not survive final cuts. Watson found himself in a similar position in Houston , where a deep receiving group forced the Texans to make difficult decisions.

Reports from Houston's final roster moves confirmed that Watson was among the players released. Hardman's release may have been the most surprising simply because of his history. The former Chiefs speedster and three-time Super Bowl champion was cut by Buffalo despite his championship pedigree.

The average NFL career is short

The cuts highlight a reality that every NFL player understands but few fans truly appreciate. The average NFL career lasts only a few years. One season, a player may be catching passes on the sport's biggest stage. The next, he may be fighting for a roster spot during the final week of the preseason.

Unlike guaranteed contracts in other professional sports, NFL careers are often determined by age, injuries, salary-cap considerations, roster depth, and the emergence of younger players. Sometimes a player declines, and sometimes the team simply finds someone cheaper. Often, it has nothing to do with what the player accomplished in the past.

Perhaps the most striking aspect of these moves is how recent their championship contributions feel. Hardman will forever be remembered in Kansas City for catching one of the most important touchdowns in franchise history. Valdes-Scantling delivered key postseason plays when the Chiefs needed them most. Watson was a trusted role player on a team that reached the top of the sport. Yet none of that guaranteed future employment.

Their stories aren't over yet

The good news for all three veterans is that roster cuts are rarely the final chapter. Injuries will occur. Practice squads will change. Teams will search for experienced depth as the season unfolds.

Valdes-Scantling, Watson, and Hardman all possess something coaches value: experience in meaningful games. Between them, they have played in conference championship games, Super Bowls , and high-pressure playoff situations. That experience could make them attractive additions for teams seeking veteran help later in the year.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling was released by the Dallas Cowboys, Justin Watson was cut by the Houston Texans, and Mecole Hardman was let go by the Buffalo Bills as teams trimmed their rosters ahead of the regular season. Just a few years ago, all three were important contributors on a championship roster. Today, all three are free agents. That is the NFL.
From champions to roster casualties

The Chiefs' receiving corps was never viewed as the most talented group in football, but it was good enough to help Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid capture a Super Bowl. Valdes-Scantling delivered some of the biggest catches of Kansas City's postseason run. Watson carved out a role as a reliable depth receiver and special teams contributor. Hardman authored one of the most memorable moments in franchise history when he caught the game-winning touchdown in overtime of Super Bowl LVIII.

Those plays are forever, but roster spots are not. Valdes-Scantling entered training camp with Dallas hoping to carve out a role in a crowded receiver room, but ultimately did not survive final cuts. Watson found himself in a similar position in Houston , where a deep receiving group forced the Texans to make difficult decisions.

Reports from Houston's final roster moves confirmed that Watson was among the players released. Hardman's release may have been the most surprising simply because of his history. The former Chiefs speedster and three-time Super Bowl champion was cut by Buffalo despite his championship pedigree.
The average NFL career is short

The cuts highlight a reality that every NFL player understands but few fans truly appreciate. The average NFL career lasts only a few years. One season, a player may be catching passes on the sport's biggest stage. The next, he may be fighting for a roster spot during the final week of the preseason.

Unlike guaranteed contracts in other professional sports, NFL careers are often determined by age, injuries, salary-cap considerations, roster depth, and the emergence of younger players. Sometimes a player declines, and sometimes the team simply finds someone cheaper. Often, it has nothing to do with what the player accomplished in the past.

Perhaps the most striking aspect of these moves is how recent their championship contributions feel. Hardman will forever be remembered in Kansas City for catching one of the most important touchdowns in franchise history. Valdes-Scantling delivered key postseason plays when the Chiefs needed them most. Watson was a trusted role player on a team that reached the top of the sport. Yet none of that guaranteed future employment.
Their stories aren't over yet
The good news for all three veterans is that roster cuts are rarely the final chapter. Injuries will occur. Practice squads will change. Teams will search for experienced depth as the season unfolds.

Valdes-Scantling, Watson, and Hardman all possess something coaches value: experience in meaningful games. Between them, they have played in conference championship games, Super Bowls , and high-pressure playoff situations. That experience could make them attractive additions for teams seeking veteran help later in the year.

The Chiefs coaching staff decided to prioritize special teams contributions over flat-out better wide receiver play for the final spot in the position room.

articles.title: Taylor Swift's new married life hits a snag as football creates tension with Travis Kelce
articles.standfirst: Football is reportedly testing the couple's newlywed routine.
articles.summary: Football is reportedly testing the couple's newlywed routine.
articles.body:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce may still be in the honeymoon phase, but their new married life is reportedly already being tested by the demands of football.

According to the Daily Mail, Swift has become frustrated by how much of Kelce's time is being consumed by the NFL as the Kansas City Chiefs prepare for another season.

The issue isn't said to be a lack of support for his career. Instead, the strain comes from how quickly their schedules have become difficult to align after marriage.

Taylor Swift is reportedly struggling with NFL demands

A source claimed Swift had hoped married life would give the couple more uninterrupted time together.

"Taylor knew what she was signing up for, but she didn't realize how quickly football would take over again," the source said.

That reality has reportedly been difficult after the pair spent more time together around their wedding and honeymoon period.

The source added: "She's happy for him and incredibly supportive, but there are moments when she feels like she barely sees him."

Kelce's responsibilities with Kansas City include training, meetings, travel and preparation, leaving far less flexibility than during the offseason.

Football becomes an early test for the newlyweds

The tension reportedly isn't serious enough to suggest a major problem in the marriage, but it has forced Swift and Kelce to adjust expectations.

"They're figuring it out as they go," the source said. "This is their first real test as husband and wife."

Swift has spent much of their relationship accommodating Kelce's NFL calendar , while Kelce has also traveled extensively to support her career.

Marriage hasn't removed those pressures.

Instead, the couple are reportedly confronting the same scheduling challenges with a new level of expectation around how much time they should spend together.

That makes football less of a crisis than an obstacle they now have to manage.

Swift is said to remain supportive of Kelce's career , but the beginning of another demanding NFL season has apparently reminded both of them that married life won't automatically create more time together.

For now, the challenge is finding a balance before the season becomes even busier.

articles.title: Matching jackets! Patrick and Brittany Mahomes completely transform into Backstreet Boys for her 31st birthday
articles.standfirst: Patrick Mahomes pulls out all the stops for Brittany
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes pulls out all the stops for Brittany
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes didn't need a long message to make his feelings clear as wife Brittany Mahomes celebrated her 31st birthday.

The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback kept his Instagram tribute simple “Happy Birthday! Love you Forever” while the couple’s weekend celebrations told the rest of the story.

Brittany shared a series of photos from the occasion, including a night at the Backstreet Boys’ “Into the Millennium” residency at the Sphere in Las Vegas.

She and Mahomes leaned into the theme by wearing matching blue-and-white varsity jackets featuring the band’s name, along with white caps and blue-tinted sunglasses. “31,” Brittany wrote alongside the carousel.

The concert photos quickly became one of the highlights of the celebration, but the birthday weekend also included quieter family moments and a look back at the life the couple has built together.

Family takes center stage

Several of the photos showed Brittany posing in front of a shimmering gold backdrop with a neon “Happy Birthday” sign and oversized metallic “31” balloons.

Mahomes joined her for one picture and kissed her on the cheek, while another image showed a three-tier birthday cake decorated with a printed family portrait.

His own birthday post also featured the couple with their three children Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 19 months. The family-focused tribute fits a relationship that began long before Mahomes became one of the most recognizable players in the NFL.

The two first met in Texas and eventually started dating as teenagers. Mahomes recalled their early relationship in Netflix’s “Quarterback” documentary.

“She was a grade above me. I was the best friend in the friendzone forever,” he said.

He also remembered giving Brittany a rose while they were still friends.

“I was getting the rose as a joke, but like kind of as a joke,” Mahomes said.

Brittany had a different reaction: “He thought it was a joke and I thought it was the cutest thing in the world,” she said.

Patrick Mahomes still makes time for Brittany

The timing of Brittany ’s birthday comes as Mahomes prepares for another demanding NFL season.

The Chiefs quarterback recently explained how limited communication can become during training camp, when players stay at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph.

“St. Joe’s dorm rooms, man, you don’t get a lot of text messages,” Mahomes said. “I just try to make sure I text Brittany. If I text Brittany, I’m usually in a good spot.”

That consistency has followed the couple from high school to marriage in 2022 and now into life with three children.

Brittany ’s 31st birthday may have included a flashy Las Vegas backdrop and matching Backstreet Boys jackets, but Mahomes ’ message was much simpler. After all these years, the sentiment remains the same.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes drives Patrick Mahomes crazy showing toned legs winning the athletic race at home
articles.standfirst: Brittany Mahomes is making a strong case for being the fittest Mahomes at home
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes is making a strong case for being the fittest Mahomes at home
articles.body:
If anyone thought Patrick was the most fit person in the Mahomes household, they might have to rethink that. Brittany is leading the race for who really holds the athletic crown at home. ​ ​Sports have always been a basic part of the Mahomes household since both have been athletes their entire lives, making it natural for them to share a passion for fitness. After Brittany's visit to the Arrowhead field, it was clear that the Chiefs quarterback's wife has been putting in extra hours with the weights.

Brittany's latest look made that fitness work hard to miss

Brittany Mahomes showed off her toned thighs in tiny shorts while posing with her family on the sidelines at Arrowhead Stadium . She arrived in a coordinated light-wash denim set, wearing a cropped jacket with drop shoulders, dark contrast buttons and button-flap chest pockets. Underneath, she wore a white top with a patterned neckband, completing the look with high-waisted denim shorts that rode up her thighs.

For Brittany, exercise is vital, and she has said it multiple times on social media. It is not only about looking good, but about feeling better from within and having the energy to do everything she sets her mind to. She is often seen posting workout content with her personal trainer, especially during her pregnancies, when she continued to look strong . Exercise has also helped her deal with her back injury.

Patrick has been putting in the work too

Patrick has been very committed to the recovery process following his injury and has paid close attention to his strength. At this point in other offseasons, he might have been getting attention for his dad bod, but this time, Patrick stepped up his work and trained extra hard to be ready to return with the Chiefs. ​ ​Still, many believe Brittany remains the most powerful Mahomes in the house. ​

articles.title: Travis Kelce warns Patrick Mahomes: "I still haven’t played the perfect game”
articles.standfirst: Veteran tight end insists there's another level to reach
articles.summary: Veteran tight end insists there's another level to reach
articles.body:
Travis Kelce could spend the rest of his career talking about everything he has already won. Instead, as Patrick Mahomes prepares to return and the Kansas City Chiefs reset for another season, the veteran tight end is focused on something he still believes is missing and that's perfection.

“I’ve had a lot of success in the NFL, but I’m still reaching for that perfection,” Kelce told Vogue. “I still haven’t played the perfect game.”

It's a striking standard for a player who has already been part of three Super Bowl-winning teams and one of the most successful quarterback-tight end partnerships of his generation.

Kelce , now entering his 14th NFL season, made clear that Mahomes ’ return has given him another jolt of motivation after the quarterback missed time last season with a torn ACL.

“Year 14, baby, I’m fired up,” Kelce said. “Every year there’s a chance to do something special, but especially coming into this year, getting Pat [Mahomes] back and wiping the slate clean.”

That “clean slate” appears to be more important to Kelce than the weight of the Chiefs ’ recent history.

Kelce not treating Year 14 like victory lap

At 36, Kelce is at a stage when retirement questions naturally follow every season. His own comments, however, sound far more like those of a player still chasing another peak.

“I love coming to the building every day,” he said. “I know how special this team is, so I’m excited to get this thing rolling and for the chance to give the fans what they deserve.”

Kansas City’s success with Mahomes and Kelce has raised expectations to an extraordinary level, but that is exactly the environment the tight end still seems to embrace.

He doesn't sound interested in simply extending his career but rather wants another season that feels complete.

Another way to chase impossible standard

Kelce explained that mentality through his passion for golf, which he believes feeds the same competitive instincts that have shaped his football career.

“Golf kind of checks off a lot of boxes for me,” he said. “One, it keeps that competitiveness in me.”

He continued: “Not only with my friends or whomever I’m playing with, but also that inner competitiveness. Of trying to strive for something and reaching for the peak.”

The lesson, Kelce said, is that the peak itself may never fully arrive.

“Ultimately, you never get there, but you keep at it,” he said. “And that’s all sports, you know? It doesn’t matter how good you are already.”

That philosophy explains why Mahomes ’ return matters so much. Kelce has already built a Hall of Fame-caliber résumé and experienced nearly every high the NFL can offer.

Yet entering Year 14, he is still looking forward rather than backward. Three championships have not satisfied him. Apparently, neither has any game he has played so far.
